# Requirements for the internal app

Faro is a model for the company’s internal goals app, plus a demo; it never holds real data. The internal team copies its code and plugs in their own platform. Some things that app must do, Faro doesn’t build: because that platform provides the machinery (sign-in, single sign-on, time zones done properly, the scale and safety of real data, telling people things, keeping and erasing data, audit, monitoring), or because they only matter in a company the size of the real one (its organisation, delegates, a planning round). Each is written here instead, so the rebuild has the rule even though Faro has no code for it.

Each page says why, the rule, what Faro does today (and where it falls short), worked examples (those marked **Faro today** are run against Faro’s code), acceptance checks, and the nearest stage of [the rebuild kit](../../rebuild/README.md).

| Requirement | What it says | Nearest stage |

Sign-in and access](r1-sign-in-and-access.md) | Everyone signs in; the signed-in person is who acts; the server enforces who may see and change what, with the rules Faro’s shared actions already enforce in code. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |
| [R2. Company single sign-on](r2-single-sign-on.md) | People sign in through the company’s identity provider, are matched to their person record by a stable id, and lose access the day they leave the company. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |
| [R3. Time zones](r3-time-zones.md) | Store real moments, count weeks and days in the workspace’s home zone, show every time in the viewer’s own zone, and give reviews a time and a zone. | [Stage 1: the core rules](../../rebuild/stage-1-core-rules.md) |

Scale and safety](r4-scale-and-safety.md) | 15,000 people: the rules’ results kept as summary rows on the server, every growing list paged, page-load budgets checked in CI, backups that are restored for real, migrations rehearsed, and the master key used only where nothing else will do. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |

Notifications and the weekly habit](r5-notifications-and-habits.md) | Telling people things, through the company’s email, Slack, Teams and phones: asks at once, one reminder before the review, a weekly digest in set words, check-in from a notification, and the habit rules: never shame, streaks that forgive, one measure of the habit. Also one sign-in with a role per workspace, and feedback kept per workspace. | [Stage 3: the core screens and journeys](../../rebuild/stage-3-core-screens.md) |
| [R6a. The organisation](r6a-organisation.md) | Teams form a tree fed from the company directory, people have managers, goal levels are set per workspace, and every list, count, Home and review can be scoped to a part of the company. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |
| [R6b. Delegates](r6b-delegates.md) | An owner, their manager or an admin names a delegate who checks in and answers asks for the owner’s goals while they are away; it is recorded as the delegate acting for the owner, and the owner stays the owner. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |

The planning round](r6c-planning-round.md) | Next cycle’s goals are drafted, proposed and agreed in a planning round before the cycle starts; a goal counts nowhere until it is agreed, and the cycle starts with the agreed set. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |

Data retention, privacy and erasure](r7-retention-and-privacy.md) | What is personal data, how long each kind of record is kept, what a leaver’s record keeps, and how a person sees everything held about them or has it erased. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |
| [R8. Audit](r8-audit.md) | A record of who did what that no one can change, with admins’ exports and every AI token’s use in it, kept 7 years, and exported by those allowed to. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |

Large imports, a server-side job](r11-large-imports.md) | An import of tens of thousands of rows is a job on the server (R-L1 to R-L6): checked there by the same rules, saved in one transaction or in batches that end in one state, with Undo kept per import, and the browser’s preview only advice. | [Stage 2: the core data and the change engine](../../rebuild/stage-2-core-data.md) |

## How they fit the rest of the spec

- The rules about who may do what, the status rules and the change engine are Faro’s own and live once, in the code ([the core rules](../../core/rules/README.md)). These pages don’t restate them; they say where the internal app must enforce them, and how.
- Faro’s own requirements, with their tests and journeys, are in [the core requirements](../../core/requirements.md). These have acceptance checks instead, for the internal team to automate on their platform.
